# Draft:Wyldwood Renaissance Festival

----
= Wyldwood Renaissance Festival =
Wyldwood Renaissance Festival (commonly known as Wyldwood RenFest) is an annual Renaissance and fantasy-themed festival held at Kirkleatham Showground in Redcar, North Yorkshire, England. The festival celebrates medieval and Renaissance culture with a strong emphasis on British folklore, myth, and fantasy. The first event is scheduled for 29–31 May 2026.
Overview
Wyldwood RenFest combines elements of traditional Renaissance Faires with the unique folklore and fantasy heritage of the British Isles. The event offers a blend of living history demonstrations, artisan markets, live entertainment, and hands-on activities for all ages. It also prides itself on being highly inclusive and accessible, aiming to make history and folklore engaging and welcoming for visitors from all backgrounds.
History
Founded by Laura Lascaris and her team under the company Bodkin Events Ltd, Wyldwood RenFest was conceived in 2023 with the vision of creating a UK-based Renaissance festival inspired by both historical tradition and imaginative folklore. The festival also received early support from sponsors including Nidhoggr Mead Co., Wolf and Witch Night Market, Pagans of the North and local authorities welcomed its arrival as both a cultural and economic boost for the region.
The event is designed to offer a balanced mix of historical accuracy and creative fantasy, giving equal space to reenactors, artisan traders, performers, and fantasy enthusiasts.
Attractions and Activities
The festival offers a variety of experiences designed to appeal to both history enthusiasts and families:
* Living History Displays: Reenactors in period dress demonstrate medieval crafts, combat, and daily life.
* Marketplace: Over 100 traders offering handmade wares including costumes, jewellery, weaponry, home décor, and food.
* Live Entertainment: Traditional folk musicians, minstrels, and theatrical groups perform on dedicated stages and as roving entertainers.
* Workshops: Visitors can take part in interactive sessions such as blacksmithing, weaving, archery, and storytelling.
* Children’s Activities: Crafting stations, medieval-themed games, and immersive storytelling designed especially for young attendees.
* Camping: On-site tent-only camping area to maintain a period-appropriate setting for overnight guests.
Unlike some medieval festivals, Wyldwood RenFest deliberately includes mythological and fantasy themes, encouraging creative costumes, cosplay, and imaginative play alongside more traditional historical presentations.
Location
Wyldwood RenFest is held at Kirkleatham Showground, a 54-acre site in Redcar, North Yorkshire, chosen for its expansive grounds, historic character, and proximity to local transport links. The venue offers ample space for the festival’s marketplace, live stages, encampments, and visitor facilities, including dedicated parking areas and camping zones.
Accessibility
The festival places strong emphasis on accessibility and inclusion. The site design includes separate disabled parking, accessible toilet facilities, and sensory-friendly spaces. The event also accepts the [https://www.accesscard.online/ Access Card] scheme, offering support for disabled visitors and their carers. Volunteers and staff are trained to assist visitors with a range of needs, reflecting the organisers’ commitment to creating a welcoming environment for all.
Community and Ethos
Wyldwood RenFest is rooted in a community-driven ethos, fostering collaboration with local businesses, artisans, and charities. The event aims to promote not only entertainment but also education, sustainability, and cultural appreciation.
Organisers also implement eco-friendly policies, encouraging traders to use recyclable, reusable, or compostable materials and working with waste management services to reduce the festival’s environmental footprint.
Organisation
The festival is organised by Bodkin Events Ltd, supported by a core team overseeing logistics, safety, finance, and entertainment. The event collaborates closely with local authorities and emergency services to ensure a smooth and secure experience for all visitors. The team also works with external suppliers and sponsors to enhance both the festival’s infrastructure and atmosphere.
Future Plans
Following its debut in 2026, the organisers of Wyldwood RenFest plan to establish the event as a permanent fixture in the UK festival calendar. Long-term goals include expanding its performance roster, increasing the scale of its re-enactments, and potentially introducing seasonal sister events such as a winter festival.
